title: Top Metronome Alternatives for Usage-Based Billing (2026)
summary: Start with Lago Cloud for a prepaid AI wallet, then compare Metronome alternatives on contracts, payments, deployment, and cost.
body_markdown:
[Lago Cloud](https://getlago.com/pricing) is the managed starting point for an AI company that needs a prepaid wallet, usage rates by model, customer-specific terms, and invoices. It runs in US and EU regions, and its native payment integrations include Stripe Payments, Adyen, and GoCardless. The app or gateway still enforces access at zero credits.


Metronome is a serious alternative for that advanced workflow. It has depth in rate cards, prepaid commits, contracts, and spend alerts. Stripe[completed its acquisition](https://stripe.com/newsroom/news/stripe-completes-metronome-acquisition) on January 14, 2026, so buyers should check its current integration, export, and commercial terms.[Compare the same prepaid AI wallet](https://getlago.com/blog/stripe-billing-metronome-lago) in Lago Cloud, basic Stripe Billing Meters, and Metronome.


These alternatives solve different parts of the billing workflow. Test your events, wallet balance, contract terms, invoice, and payment path before ranking them.


## Lago


[Lago Cloud](https://getlago.com/pricing) meters and rates usage, manages prepaid wallets, and invoices customers as a managed service. Teams needing deployment control can self-host Lago’s open-source edition. Real-time balance access is plan dependent, and the application or gateway enforces hard access limits.


Lago operates the application, databases, event pipeline, monitoring, and upgrades on Lago Cloud. Your team configures pricing and connects usage, payment, and finance tools. Self-hosting is an additional option when your team needs to run billing on its own infrastructure.


Payment choice is a practical distinction. Lago has native Stripe Payments, Adyen, and GoCardless integrations; Cashfree and MoneyHash are community connectors, and other processors need custom work. Metronome’s[external payment gate](https://docs.metronome.com/guides/customers-billing/optimize-customer-experience/prepaid-balance-thresholds) can work with another gateway when your team handles payment and credit release. Its native Stripe path is simpler. Compare integration and reconciliation work, not ownership alone.


On the metering side, Lago supports high-cardinality usage events with filters and dimensions, and its aggregation types go beyond the basics: count, count unique, latest, max, sum, weighted sum, and custom aggregation for pricing logic that doesn't fit a template. Ingestion runs through REST, batch imports, SDKs, Kafka, Redpanda, Kinesis, or S3, the same foundation we walk through in[how to build a usage-based billing system](https://getlago.com/blog/usage-based-billing-system) . Wallets and prepaid credits are native, with configured alerts that do not authorize spend synchronously; your app or gateway enforces hard limits.


**Best for:** AI, API, and SaaS teams that need managed usage billing, prepaid credits, customer-specific rates, and invoices, with a choice of supported payment processors. Teams with deployment-control requirements can also evaluate self-hosted Lago.


**Finance requirements to test:** compare contract approvals, invoice reconciliation, and revenue reporting against your finance team's workflow.[Lago revenue recognition](https://getlago.com/platform/revenue-recognition) is a Premium private beta for draft accrual reports that finance reconciles. Lago connects to payment providers; global collection and FX depend on the provider you choose.


**Pricing:**[Lago Cloud Launch](https://getlago.com/pricing) has no minimum commitment. Its first 5 million accepted production events and first $100,000 of processed billings are separate, one-time free allowances. Once each allowance is exhausted, events cost $20 per million and billings cost 0.7%. Scale starts at a $12,000 annual minimum, with billing rates from 0.6% and event terms set by agreement. Enterprise is custom. Self-hosted open source has no license fee; infrastructure and operations cost extra.


## Orb


Orb is a purpose-built usage-based billing platform for pricing iteration, usage ingestion, credits, alerts, and invoicing. It was acquired by Adyen, closing July 1, 2026, alongside Adyen's acquisition of Talon.One. Orb says current customers should see no immediate changes to availability, support, or pricing, and that it remains committed to interoperability.


Orb is strong on pricing-launch speed and has a genuinely useful simulation product for modeling pricing changes before you ship them, something Lago doesn't offer as a packaged UI today. Its alerting is fast, evaluated roughly every three minutes with notifications inside five.


The tradeoff is the same shape as Metronome's, just with a different owner. Orb is a closed, hosted platform, and its public pricing points to custom packages rather than transparent per-transaction rates. Adyen's ownership raises the same long-term neutrality question that Stripe's ownership of Metronome does: ownership alone does not establish processor restrictions; ask which integrations work today and what switching requires. We've covered[what the Adyen acquisition means for teams evaluating Orb](https://getlago.com/blog/orb-adyen-acquisition-lago-alternative) and a full[Lago vs Orb comparison](https://getlago.com/blog/lago-vs-orb) in more depth elsewhere.


**Best for:** product-led infrastructure and AI companies that want deep metering and pricing-simulation tooling and are comfortable with a closed platform and a sales-led pricing conversation.


**Pricing:** custom, quote-based.


## Chargebee


Chargebee is a mature SaaS revenue platform covering subscriptions, entitlements-based usage billing, invoicing, payment workflows, and revenue recognition, with documented support for up to 100 million usage events a month.


It's a solid choice if revenue recognition and finance-team workflows are your primary requirement and you're comfortable with a hosted, closed platform. Chargebee's public documentation shows no open-source or self-hosted option, so if deployment control is a requirement rather than a preference, it sits in the same category as Metronome and Orb on that axis. See our[Lago vs Chargebee comparison](https://getlago.com/blog/lago-vs-chargebee) for a closer look at where the two diverge.


**Best for:** finance-led teams that want strong RevRec and invoicing workflows out of the box and don't need self-hosting.


**Pricing:** tiered plans plus custom enterprise pricing; contact sales for usage-based tiers.


## OpenMeter (now part of Kong)


OpenMeter is an open-source metering and billing platform. Kong announced its acquisition of OpenMeter on September 3, 2025, and it's being folded into Kong Konnect's metering and billing product. OpenMeter remains open source, and it has some of the strongest real-time entitlement and access-check capabilities in this list, with documented support for limits, quotas, and notifications enforced in real time rather than after the fact.


The open question is the same one that shows up whenever an independent tool gets absorbed into a larger platform: OpenMeter's standalone commercial story is transitioning into Kong's, and its public pricing now routes to Kong or to a sales conversation instead of a transparent, standalone rate.


**Best for:** teams that specifically need real-time usage-based access enforcement, particularly around API and gateway monetization, and are comfortable adopting it as part of the broader Kong platform.


**Pricing:** contact sales, post-acquisition.


## Flexprice


Flexprice is a developer-first monetization platform aimed at AI-native and SaaS teams, built as an open-core project under an AGPLv3 license. It's the closest thing to a direct open-source, developer-first competitor to Lago, with strong support for credit grants, prepaid and promotional credits, and top-ups.


Flexprice is newer and has a smaller track record at scale than Lago, Metronome, or Orb, so the evaluation question is less about philosophy, since it shares Lago's open-source and developer-first premise, and more about maturity, ecosystem, and how much of your pricing model its current feature set actually covers today.


**Best for:** early-stage AI and SaaS teams that want an open-core, developer-first billing layer and are comfortable evaluating a younger platform.


**Pricing:** not publicly listed; contact sales.


## Sequence


Sequence is a revenue platform for flexible pricing, contracts, invoicing, revenue recognition, and CRM and accounting workflows, with a public Growth tier at $799 a month for startups under $1 million in ARR, plus bespoke Core and Scale packaging above that.


Sequence leans toward finance and revenue operations rather than developer-first usage metering, and its published Growth plan includes usage metering, so test capacity and configuration with your workload. It's worth a look if your billing pain is mostly around contracts, quotes, and revenue recognition rather than metering raw usage at scale.


**Best for:** revenue and finance teams outgrowing basic subscription tooling who need better contract and RevRec workflows, after testing the metering requirements they actually have.


**Pricing:** Growth tier at $799/month under $1M ARR; custom Core and Scale tiers above that.


## Stripe Billing


Stripe Billing handles subscriptions and basic usage billing through Meters. Its[pay-as-you-go rate](https://stripe.com/billing/pricing) is 0.7% of Billing volume, and its pricing page says **up to 100 million meter events per month are included** . Eligibility, event counting, and overage terms are not explained there. That allowance does not provide the live prepaid wallet being compared here.


Stripe offers Metronome for more advanced prepaid, contract, and dimensional workflows. Moving from Billing Meters to Metronome is a[documented migration](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based/migrate-to-metronome) , not a plan toggle. For that buyer decision, use our[Lago vs Stripe Billing comparison](https://getlago.com/blog/lago-vs-stripe) and the three-way wallet example.


**Best for:** teams whose usage can be counted and invoiced after the period without a live prepaid access decision. Stripe Billing also supports off-Stripe payments; confirm the integration and terms for your region.


**Pricing:** 0.7% of billing volume (pay-as-you-go), or monthly tiers.


## Is Lago right for you?


Choose Lago Cloud if your next offer needs usage rates, prepaid credits, customer-specific terms, and invoices on a managed platform. Ask Lago and Metronome to demonstrate the same offer, from the first usage event through a top-up, invoice, and payment reconciliation.


Compare the total cost for your event volume, processed billings, integrations, and support. Lago Cloud Launch charges on both billings and events after its separate free allowances, so use the[current plan terms](https://getlago.com/pricing) in your calculation. Add infrastructure and operating costs only when evaluating the self-hosted option.


The demo should show who operates billing, how credits reach the invoice, and what your application and payment provider must handle.[Walk through your pricing model with Lago](https://getlago.com/book-a-demo) to confirm the Cloud plan and integration scope.


If you're comparing more than Metronome, our other alternative guides cover[Stripe Billing](https://getlago.com/blog/top-7-alternatives-to-stripe-billing-for-usage-based-billing) ,[Recurly](https://getlago.com/blog/top-7-alternatives-to-recurly-for-usage-based-billing) , and[Chargebee](https://getlago.com/blog/chargebee-alternative) in the same format.


### Key takeaways


- Stripe completed its acquisition of Metronome on January 14, 2026, which means buyers should verify Metronome’s current integrations, data export, and commercial terms under Stripe ownership.
- Most Metronome alternatives, including Orb, Chargebee, and Sequence, are closed, hosted platforms with no public self-hosting option; Lago, OpenMeter, and Flexprice are the open-source options in this category.
- Test payment options as an integration, not an ownership claim: Lago has native Stripe Payments, Adyen, and GoCardless connectors, community Cashfree and MoneyHash connectors, and a custom path for others. Metronome documents an external payment gate with custom credit-release work. Verify the payment and reconciliation flow for each provider.
- Lago Cloud runs billing infrastructure for teams that want a managed service. Teams that need deployment control can self-host Lago's open-source product.
